title: unwith
summary: Removes with blocks, proving every name binds to what it bound before
intro: Read this when you want a with statement gone without a name silently changing meaning. --plan names, for every with in a file or a project, whether it can be removed and exactly why not; --apply rewrites through the compile gate, then re-indexes a copy of the DB and rolls back if any reference binds elsewhere. Since 1.52.2 the with fixes of lint --fix (fix all, the IDE's Fix all in unit) carry the same after proof and are declined when a binding would change; since 1.52.3 that proof re-indexes a scratch copy of the file and never writes your source, also not on a dry run.

help:
drag-lint unwith --db [--in [--line ]] (--plan | --apply --project ) [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ] [--library-db |none] [--exclude-under

]... [--no-backup] [--build-config ] [--no-preprocess] [--json|--format json] - remove with blocks, proved binding by binding

drag-lint lint  <path>       [--profile <name>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>] [--rule <id>|help] [--disable id1,id2] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--json] [--labels] [--no-preprocess] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--build-config <name>] [--no-budget]
[--db <index.sqlite>]  (a store enables the type-aware and ancestry checks, and the project
rules for this file, incl. the ON opt-in discarded-effect-free-result; the OFF opt-in ones run only under --rule)
<path> may be a FOLDER: every scanned .pas/.inc/.dpr gets the same checks as lint <file> (their union)
[--output <file>]: with --json or --format sarif the document is written to the file instead of stdout (a note on stderr).
[--project-rules]  (also run doc-drift/missing-doc for this file -- OFF by default:
they rebuild facts PER DECL, ~16ms each, and can exceed the IDE's 8s budget)
[--stand-in-for <realpath>]  (analyse <path>'s TEXT as though it were <realpath>:
for editor buffers snapshotted to a temp file -- fixes store membership, file id,
unit-name and the reported path)
drag-lint lint  --project <file.dproj> [--build-config <name>] [--rule unit-not-in-dpr|unit-not-in-library|help] [--json]
drag-lint lint  --in <f.pas> --fix [--fix-line <L> --fix-rule <id>] [--fix-naming] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (AUTOFIX one file; --apply keeps a .bak beside each file it writes unless --no-backup)
DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply: it reports what it would change and writes no source file.
--fix-line + --fix-rule together narrow the fix to ONE finding; omit both to
apply every fixable finding in the file. Only rules whose catalog entry has
"fixable": true are ever applied -- see `drag-lint rules --json`.
--fix-naming: kept for compatibility, a no-op since 1.37.0 -- every fix, the naming renames (across
every owning project) included, is ON by default; only "autofix_off": [...] in drag-lint-lint.json withholds one;
with it the run still prints "rename-local: <N>" (stderr) for the single-project renames.
This is what the IDE Structure form's right-click Fix it / Fix all in unit run.
